clue.text: First and last from sea bird, last and first for G

definitions.note: G stands for Gallery throughout this themed puzzle, as 18 down reveals

indicators.note: the first and last letters are taken away from the bird's name, leaving its middle

parts.note: a puffin is a sea bird
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
I is the Roman numeral one, the first number

explanation.surface: Instructions for picking letters from a seabird's name and reversing their order for a G.
explanation.walkthrough: The G in each themed clue is a gallery (see 18 down). 'last and first' supply Z (end of the alphabet) and I (one) in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uffizi in Florence is one of the world's great art galleries.

clue.text: Didn't Annan exist?

parts.note: Kofi Annan, as UN Secretary-General, was a man of the United Nations; the word for someone officially erased from existence splits into that organisation's abbreviation and a human being

explanation.surface: A doubter questions whether the former UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan was ever real.
explanation.definitionFit: An unperson, from Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, is someone officially treated as never having existed.

clue.text: Meal cut right in half when raised to primitive faith object

indicators.note: the meal and the abbreviation for right are placed inside the other word
in a down clue, raised means the word half is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
tea is an afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: A meal is cut and halved, then offered up to some primitive idol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when raised' turns HALF into FLAH, which then takes TEA and RT inside it, after its first three letters. 'cut' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief that the world is a flat disc is the archetypal primitive, discredited article of faith.

clue.text: Animal doctor, perhaps, rushed noisily around

parts.note: zoo is a common prefix and word for animals kept for show, as in zoo animals
MED is short for medic, of whom a doctor is one example

explanation.surface: A vet hurried, with plenty of noise, around the place.
explanation.definitionFit: To zoom is to move fast with a loud humming or buzzing sound.

clue.text: Cover for strike-breaking poet

parts.note: a scab is a strike-breaker, a worker who crosses the picket line
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: Someone is looking for an alibi for a poet who broke a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath that covers a sword blade.

clue.text: Subject of initial-for instance Hiram

definitions.meaning: the first letter written as an initial abbreviates a person's first given name
Hiram is an example of a forename given at baptism

explanation.definitionFit: A Christian name is a first or given name, which an initial stands for, and Hiram is one.

clue.text: See 19
Expression of regret for a shortage

parts.note: a lack is a shortage

explanation.surface: Someone sighs over running short of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an old-fashioned cry of sorrow, as in alas and alack.

clue.text: Dredge the river Swan?

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Should the river swan be dredged?
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a British river (there is one in Scotland and one along the Welsh border).
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging a channel makes it deeper by scooping out the bed.

clue.text: Fuss over projection of image at G

definitions.note: G stands for Gallery in this themed puzzle

indicators.note: in this across clue the fuss comes after, so it is placed over the other piece

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the business of projecting an image
ado means fuss, as in much ado

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over how a picture should be projected at a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The G is a gallery, as 18 down explains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prado in Madrid is Spain's national art museum.

clue.text: G's number among stuff from the past

definitions.note: read as G is: the G is a gallery in this themed puzzle

indicators.note: the number is placed among the letters of the other word, inside it

parts.note: heritage is what is handed down from the past
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A gallery's catalogue number appears among items from history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'G's' means 'G is'; G is a gallery throughout (18 down).
explanation.definitionFit: The Hermitage in St Petersburg is one of the largest art museums in the world.

clue.text: Bisexual woman with plan for the Dior exhibition

parts.note: her refers to a woman
a map is a plan

indicators.note: an exhibition shows things off, so the letters of the fashion house phrase are put on display in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman has a plan for a Dior fashion show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhibition' signals HRODITE, a rearrangement of THE DIOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermaphrodite has both male and female sexual organs, bisexual in the biological sense.

clue.text: Line of seats expensive, said the pretty little creature.

indicators.note: said tells us the words are spoken, giving a sound like the answer

parts.note: a row is a line of seats; dear means expensive

explanation.surface: A theatregoer complains that a row of seats is pricey while admiring a pretty creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small, graceful deer of Europe and Asia.

clue.text: … a bigger one does his monologue with backing from Glitter

indicators.note: backing means the pieces are all read backwards, end to start

parts.note: following on from the small deer of 11 across, a bigger deer is the elk
raps, as a rapper delivers words over a beat

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, a bigger stag performs a solo turn backed by a glam-rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 11 across: 'a bigger one' is a bigger deer, ELK. 'with backing' turns ELK RAPS round to give SPARKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sparkle is to glitter, shining with flashes of light.

clue.text: Bugbear in progress

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A persistent annoyance holds up work in progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear was originally a hobgoblin, an imaginary monster used to frighten children, like an ogre.

clue.text: The race of the race for G

definitions.meaning: the Grand ..., Britain's most famous steeplechase, is called simply that
relating to a people or nation

explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is a famous British horse race at Aintree; the London gallery (the G) also shares the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing fans call the Grand National steeplechase by its short name, and the adjective means belonging to a people.

clue.text: Silliest at any rate

definitions.meaning: the silliest person is the one with the smallest wisdom
an old-fashioned phrase meaning anyway or at least

explanation.definitionFit: The silliest is the least wise, and leastwise is a dated adverb for at least or anyway.

clue.text: Tile on top of the box?

definitions.text: Tile on top of the box?

parts.words: Tile on top of the box?
parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat and box is slang for the head, so this describes what is worn above it

explanation.surface: A roof tile sits on top of a box.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a 'tile' is a hat and the 'box' (or nut) is a person's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Headgear is anything worn on the head, such as a hat.

clue.text: Symbol of arbitrariness raised to gain attention?

definitions.meaning: acting with an overbearing, domineering manner
a palm lifted up in class to catch a teacher's eye

explanation.definitionFit: A high hand means imperious, arbitrary conduct, and a hand held up high seeks attention.

clue.text: The G in this puzzle is largely new

indicators.note: new means the letters of the word are made afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that the G featured in this puzzle is mostly brand new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' looks like 'mostly' but it is the fodder; 'new' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Every G in the themed clues stands for a gallery, an art museum such as the Tate.

clue.text: Time corroded intelligence-without it it's a G

definitions.note: G stands for Gallery in this themed puzzle

parts.note: ate, as acid ate into metal

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the brain word goes around the other piece

parts.note: brain means intelligence
taken as written

explanation.surface: Time has worn away a mind, and without it what's left is a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: BRAIN goes round IT, giving BRITAIN. The answer spans 19 across and 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tate Britain is the London art gallery on Millbank devoted to British art.

clue.text: It creates false images of OAPs

definitions.text: It creates false images of OAPs

indicators.note: false says the letters of the word images are not what they seem and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something gives a distorted picture of pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is prejudice against older people, which spreads distorted stereotypes of pensioners.

clue.text: Gin the window

definitions.meaning: G stands for Gallery in this themed puzzle, here the Paris museum
a set of overlapping slats fitted in a window opening to let air in

explanation.walkthrough: The print runs 'G in' together as 'Gin'; the clue is a double definition joined by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louvre in Paris is a famous art museum, and a louvre is a slatted shutter or vent.

clue.text: Scientist has proof, reportedly, with sign

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for a printer's proof is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a galley is a printer's proof
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A scientist presents his evidence along with a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian astronomer and physicist who championed the Copernican model.

clue.text: Siren's failure rate in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A siren's rate of failure is under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren in myth tempts sailors to their doom, an enticer.

clue.text: A theologian accepting poor poet to be one of the family

indicators.note: accepting means the theologian's letters take in the other piece

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree

indicators.note: poor means the word poet is badly formed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theologian takes in a struggling poet as one of the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges POET to OPTE, which goes inside DD.
explanation.definitionFit: An adopted child is legally taken in and becomes a full member of the household.

clue.text: One of the chosen aristocracy-fresh air's gone to their head

indicators.note: the reworked letters go in front of the aristocrats' word
fresh means the letters are made new, rearranged

parts.note: the word with its s counted as a letter
the elite is the aristocracy, the top layer of society

explanation.surface: The fresh air has gone to the heads of the aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges AIRS to ISRA, and 'gone to their head' puts it before ELITE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites are called the chosen people in the Bible.

clue.text: Express love — what's wrong about that?

indicators.note: about means the word for wrongdoing goes around the letter for love

parts.note: vice is wrongdoing
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A moralist asks what could be wrong with expressing love.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to express it.

clue.text: Hoodies of Sherwood?

parts.note: the followers of Robin Hood in Sherwood Forest, punningly called hoodies like hooded youths

explanation.surface: Young people in hooded tops roaming Sherwood Forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Merry Men were Robin Hood's band of outlaws in Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: Facing Tyneside -change course to take it in

indicators.note: the word for changing direction takes the region inside itself

parts.note: veer means change course
Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: A ship off Tyneside changes course to take something on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle in North East England, hence NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin facing layer of fine wood over cheaper material.
